requirements.title: Associating entities have selector rank and bounds with no ALLOCATABLE or POINTER attributes
requirements.definition: Within ASSOCIATE, CHANGE TEAM, or SELECT TYPE, each associating entity has the same rank as its selector. Each lower bound is the LBOUND result for the corresponding selector dimension, and each upper bound is lower bound plus extent minus one. The associating entity does not have ALLOCATABLE or POINTER.

pending.same-rank-as-selector: PENDING positive-control ASSOCIATE program using SHAPE or rank-specific source contexts to distinguish scalar, rank-one, and rank-two selectors without assuming unrelated array semantics.
pending.nondefault-lower-bound: PENDING positive-control with a selector whose lower bound is deliberately not one, asserting LBOUND of the associate name; this is non-vacuous because default bounds would not distinguish a bug.
pending.upper-bound-from-extent: PENDING positive-control with a selector section whose lower bound and extent imply an upper bound different from the selector declared upper bound, asserted with UBOUND and SIZE/shape dependencies.
pending.no-allocatable-attribute-source: PENDING source-control contrast showing ALLOCATE/deallocate or allocatable-only contexts cannot be applied to the associate name solely because the selector is allocatable; any diagnostic is filed under ALLOCATE or attribute-owner rules.
pending.no-pointer-attribute-source: PENDING source-control contrast showing pointer assignment to the associate name is not admitted merely because the selector is a pointer, except where 11.1.3.3 p5/C1101 permits pointer association context through a definable selector.

requirements.oracle: LBOUND/UBOUND/SHAPE inquiries are acceptable only because this paragraph requires the expected bounds; future plans must avoid circular use of array-section formation as the sole oracle.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source-only catalogue records pending plans only. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no processor, approves no fixture or oracle, and claims no coverage. Future ASSOCIATE fixtures must use non-vacuous selectors and sentinels: lower bounds must differ where bounds are asserted, character length must be checked with LEN rather than inferred from padded comparison, outer homonyms must start with values different from any inner assignment, and assignment through an associate name is credited only after the selector is established definable. No plan may count selector evaluations, depend on function side effects, assume a real or complex kind exists, or use compiler agreement as an oracle.

requirements.title: Associating entities have selector corank and selector cobounds for coarray selectors
requirements.definition: Within ASSOCIATE, SELECT RANK, or SELECT TYPE, each associating entity has the same corank as its selector. If the selector is a coarray, the cobounds of each codimension of the associating entity are the same as those of the selector.

requirements.title: Associating entities inherit ASYNCHRONOUS, VOLATILE, dynamic type, optional absence, and contiguity properties as specified
requirements.definition: Within ASSOCIATE, CHANGE TEAM, SELECT RANK, or SELECT TYPE, the associating entity has ASYNCHRONOUS or VOLATILE if and only if the selector is a variable and has the attribute. If polymorphic, it assumes the selector dynamic type and type parameter values. It does not have OPTIONAL; an OPTIONAL selector cannot be absent. It is contiguous if and only if the selector is contiguous.

requirements.title: Associating entities are variables but are not definable when their selectors are not definable or not permitted in definition contexts
requirements.definition: The associating entity itself is a variable. If the selector is not a definable variable, the associating entity is not definable and shall not be defined or become undefined. If a selector is not permitted in a variable definition context, neither the associate name nor any subobject of it shall appear in a variable definition context or pointer association context.

pending.definable-selector-assignment-control: PENDING positive-control ASSOCIATE with a definable variable selector initialized to a value distinct from the assigned value, assigning through the associate name and observing the selector changed.
pending.nondefinable-selector-definition-rejecte: PENDING diagnostic/control pair where the selector is a nondefinable variable (for example protected or otherwise prohibited by its owner) and the associate name is assigned; the repair changes only to a definable selector.
pending.nondefinable-selector-undefinition-rejec: PENDING diagnostic/control pair where the associate name for a nondefinable selector would become undefined, repaired by using a definable selector or removing the undefinition context.
pending.selector-not-vdc-associate-definition-re: PENDING diagnostic/control pair where the selector is not permitted in a variable definition context and only the associate name appears in such a context; the repair changes that one context or selector.
pending.selector-not-vdc-pointer-association-rej: PENDING diagnostic/control pair where the associate name or subobject appears in a pointer association context although the selector is not permitted in a variable definition context; the repair uses a selector permitted in that context.

review_rationale: batch111: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...). This batch opens Clause 11, so it establishes the shape later Clause 11 packets follow. The reviewer read all 44 base units of 11.1.1 Blocks, 11.1.2.1 Control flow in blocks, 11.1.2.2 Execution of a block, 11.1.3.1 through 11.1.3.4 the ASSOCIATE construct, and 11.1.4 the BLOCK construct in the original PDF rather than the author summary, verifying the titles from the source and confirming 44 base / 77 fine units, 42 requirements and 119 facets (all pending). The accounting claim was verified independently: the 20 numbered items R1101 in 11.1.1, R1102 through R1106 with C1101 through C1106 in 11.1.3.1, and R1107 through R1110 with C1107 through C1110 in 11.1.4 were already inventoried, so 24 non-numbered units are newly accounted, with no double count and no drop. Five permissions were adjudicated and accepted, including the 11.1.4 p3 explicit processor latitude for specification-expression evaluation order, which carries no plan asserting the processor took a particular order. Critically, the sentences of the form it is permissible to branch to an end statement only from within its construct do two things at once, permitting the inward branch and through the word only prohibiting the outward one, and the reviewer confirmed the packet captures both halves rather than losing a restriction or a permission. The attribution table was audited in full: all 30 negative rows were checked, including the R1109 row whose prohibiting words are a grammar production rather than a shall, the seven C1107 rows drawn from one prohibition list covering COMMON, EQUIVALENCE, INTENT, NAMELIST, OPTIONAL, statement functions and VALUE, the three C1101 rows and the four rows filed under 11.1.3.3 p5 that quote long compound sentences, confirming each negative isolates exactly one clause. The author's decision to treat C1104 as source-classification only was independently examined and accepted, because ordinary pointer assignment is conforming through the variable selector alternative, and 11.1.3.4's zero facets were accepted because its single note base unit and fine unit remain accounted. Decision: source-eligible, no blocking findings. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
